narrative.overview:
Love is a telegraph office. Ankit dictates, the office sets the message exactly, routes it to an address, delivers it and keeps the counterfoil as proof. Every row on these screens is the counterfoil of a message that went out — so the screens are not a dashboard of a system, they are the office's own book: a tinted board, white form paper lying on it, green printed furniture, and one vermilion datestamp struck where something needs the boss.

The system is paper-flat and hue-poor on purpose. Exactly two hues carry meaning and nothing else on the screen is ever coloured: the office's green (furniture) is what the form arrives printed with — labels, a person's name, the one data track, the ring around today — and the stamp pad's vermilion (stamp) is the state that needs Ankit. There is no third hue; a due clock time is a stamp matter, not an amber one. Every grey that carries words is tinted off the green rather than left neutral, because a neutral grey on a coloured ground reads as dirt.

Phone is the primary viewport, not the fallback. Ankit reads this standing up, several times a day, one-handed. On the phone the board shows in every gap down the whole scroll and the head of each screen sits on a bled field of board; at lg the board becomes a frame around a white sheet and the paper containers inside it flatten away, because a bordered white card on a white sheet is a box in a box.
keyCharacteristics: Two hues with one job each, and no third
Paper and board: tonal layering, zero shadow on content surfaces
Mark only where there is news; an ordinary record carries plain text
Tabular figures everywhere a column exists
Square-ish form corners (8/4/2px) and a 0px stamp
Phone-first; containers flatten on the desktop sheet

rules.name: The Two Hues Rule
rules.body: Green is the office's furniture; vermilion is the state that needs Ankit. There is no third hue — a due time is stamped, not ambered — and nothing else on the screen is ever coloured.

rules.name: The One Pad Rule
rules.body: A stamp has one ink. The green and grey stamp tones were deleted during the build; a closed record is struck through and carries no second mark.

rules.name: The 11px Floor Rule
rules.body: Nothing is set under 11px, and vermilion is text-safe at 11px (4.6:1 on board, 5.9:1 on paper). Below that it falls under 4.5:1 and stops being readable ink.

rules.name: The Tinted Grey Rule
rules.body: Every grey that carries words is tinted off the green. A neutral grey on a coloured ground reads as dirt.

rules.name: The Tabular Column Rule
rules.body: Every figure keeps its width. .num, table, time and .tabular all carry font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums, because a form's columns depend on it.

rules.name: The Six Sizes Rule
rules.body: Seven steps exist and no more (36/24/20/16/14/13/12, plus the 11px stamp). A new size is a redraw, not a decision.

rules.name: The Flatten-On-Sheet Rule
rules.body: Panels, rails and record groups are paper with a 1px edge and 4px corners on the phone, and flatten at lg (lg:rounded-none lg:border-0, often lg:bg-transparent). A bordered white card on a white sheet is a box in a box.

rules.name: The Board-In-Every-Gap Rule
rules.body: On the phone the board must show down the whole scroll: the bar, the Band and the inter-section gaps are all board. A phone screen that is white from edge to edge has lost the world.

rules.name: The Phone-First Rule
rules.body: The phone layout is the design; desktop is the secondary viewport. A decision that improves the sheet at the phone's expense is the wrong decision.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: Only a true overlay casts a shadow. A panel, a card, a row, a stamp and the sheet itself never do.

rules.name: The News-Only Stamp Rule
rules.body: A stamp strikes only where the state is news. An ordinary open record carries its age as plain text; a closed one carries only a struck-through line. A mark on every row is the status pill this world exists to refuse, whatever shape it is cut in.

rules.name: The True Ratio Rule
rules.body: Every track is drawn at its real ratio, with no stub at zero and no padded range.

rules.name: The No-Invented-Data Rule
rules.body: Every figure on every screen comes from the store. A number is never written to make a layout look finished.

rules.name: The Drawn-Icon Rule
rules.body: One 16px icon set, 1.5px stroke, currentColor, drawn in components/ui.js. No emoji, no glyph fonts, no icon packages; the brand mark is a drawn struck ring, never a letter in a box.

dos: Do strike a stamp only where the state is news — with you, held, no movement, no window — and let an ordinary open record carry its age as plain text (12px faint tabular) and a closed one carry only a struck-through line.
Do keep two hues with one job each: green (#1d5b45) for printed furniture, names, the track and the ring; vermilion (#a82a22) for the state that needs Ankit.
Do keep the 11px floor; vermilion is text-safe at 11px and nothing is set smaller.
Do give panels, rails and record groups a 1px edge on the phone and flatten them at lg (lg:rounded-none lg:border-0).
Do keep the board visible in every gap down the whole phone scroll, and keep the Band under every screen head below lg.
Do draw every track at its true ratio, with no bar at all at zero.
Do take every figure from the store.
Do set every figure tabular, and set form labels in Archivo Narrow green furniture.
Do keep the stamp-strike as the only authored motion: 90ms, steps(2, end), and honour prefers-reduced-motion, which disables it, the nav sheet and the press scale.
donts: Don't mark every row. A tinted pill repeated down a list is the exact device this world was built to replace.
Don't introduce a third hue. A due clock time is a stamp matter; warning is deliberately the same vermilion as negative.
Don't add a second stamp ink. Green and grey stamp tones were deleted; a closed line is struck through instead.
Don't put a shadow on a card, a panel, a row, the sheet or the stamp. The phone nav sheet is the only shadow in the system.
Don't nest a panel inside a panel, or leave a bordered white card on the white desktop sheet.
Don't round the stamp. It is 0px, rotated -3.4deg, and square because a form has no soft corners.
Don't use emoji, glyph fonts or an icon package; extend the drawn 16px set instead.
Don't animate an entrance on a screen opened twenty times a day, and don't shimmer or pulse a skeleton.
Don't leave a grey untinted on a coloured ground, and don't reach for navy or slate in dark mode — elevation there is lightness alone.
Don't add a font size outside the seven steps, or a radius outside 8/4/2/0.

standingWarns.why: Phone numbers are identifiers, not magnitudes; the figure rule does not apply to them.
Eight open rows against three closed ones on the secondary viewport. Padding the desktop column would cost the phone — the primary viewport — its rhythm.

detectorIgnores.why: The nested cards are the transcript's own message bubbles, the correct form for a record kept word for word; the identity tabs register as the avatars they replaced did.
The fixture documents the category default on purpose.
A rubber stamp's ink box is tight by nature; scoped to the throwaway decision fixture, not the build.
Newsprint is the dealt challenger world's declared material.

inspectorFlags.why: The emoji sit inside verbatim stored WhatsApp messages; they are the record, not decoration.

acceptedResidues: The transcript's bubbles use a 10px radius, outside the 8/4/2 band.
A stamped record row can wrap its title at 390px.
The desktop sheet ends on an empty foot.
WhatsApp template caps are unclaimed on screen.
inspection.notCanonized: These four residues and the two WARNs are recorded as carried defects, not as rules. A new surface follows the radii, the stamp rule and the flatten rule above.
